## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** Which of the following describes continuous monitoring, as distinct from continuous auditing?

A.  Internal audit's yearly test of a sample of transactions
B.  The external auditor's review of controls at year-end
C.  Management's ongoing review of whether its own controls operate
D.  A report of key performance indicators prepared for the board each quarter

**2.** In the framework of Kogan et al. (2014), a purchase order approved above its approver's limit fails a deterministic business rule. What does such a test produce?

A.  An exception
B.  An anomaly
C.  A false positive
D.  A near-duplicate

**3.** Gonzalez and Hoffman (2018) studied the prompt notification of auditees about the transactions a monitoring system flagged. What did they find when the monitoring system was weak?

A.  Notification reduced fraud by a large margin in every condition
B.  Notification had no effect on behavior
C.  Notification mainly increased false positives
D.  Notification increased the inclination to commit fraud

**4.** A query has five flag columns, each 1 or 0, and you need one row per flag with the flag's name and value. Which Power Query command produces that?

A.  Merge Queries with the Employee table
B.  Unpivot Only Selected Columns
C.  Append Queries as New
D.  Group By with the Advanced option

**5.** Before appending the exceptions, a colleague renamed the columns of the journal entry and payroll queries but left the purchase order query's date column named OrderDate. What does the appended register contain?

A.  An OrderDate column of its own, with EventDate empty for orders
B.  An error that stops the query until the column names match exactly
C.  The order dates under EventDate, because the columns are in the same order
D.  No purchase order rows, because Append drops tables whose columns differ

**6.** Why does the monitoring model keep the journal entries, purchase orders, and payroll registers as tables of their own beside the exception register?

A.  The register cannot be related to the Date table
B.  Power BI requires every unpivoted table to stay loaded
C.  The rates divide each test's exceptions by its population
D.  The drill-through page reads documents only from those tables

**7.** On the monitoring page, most tests show exceptions only in January, while one test shows exceptions in every month of every year. Which reading is most appropriate?

A.  The Date table assigns the recurring test's dates incorrectly
B.  A design flaw in the control behind the recurring test
C.  The January cluster is more serious because it is larger
D.  The recurring test should be removed as a source of noise

**8.** A role has one rule, on the CostCenter table. Which rows does it restrict?

A.  The rows of every table in the semantic model
B.  Only the rows of the CostCenter table itself
C.  The rows of any table that has a column named CostCenterID
D.  CostCenter and the tables its active relationships reach

**9.** The controller adds a department manager to the workspace as a Member, so that the manager can open the package. What will the manager see?

A.  Only the rows of the manager's own cost center
B.  Every row, because the rules do not apply to Members
C.  Nothing, until the manager is added to a security role
D.  Only the pages that the app audience includes

**10.** Why should the dynamic role not be built on the ManagerID column of Charles River's CostCenter table?

A.  The column holds names rather than the identifiers a rule needs
B.  USERPRINCIPALNAME cannot be compared with a number
C.  It names terminated employees and omits current managers
D.  A role may not read a column of a dimension table

**11.** The role in Tutorial 16.3 has a rule on Item: `USERPRINCIPALNAME () IN VALUES ( Security[UserPrincipalName] )`. What is it for?

A.  It hides the items of other cost centers from each manager
B.  It speeds up the role by filtering the largest table in the model
C.  It lets the Finance role see every item
D.  It shows no sales to anyone missing from the security table

**12.** Internal audit wants the column of hourly pay rates hidden from department managers while they still see the hours. Which feature does that?

A.  Object-level security
B.  Row-level security
C.  A sensitivity label
D.  An app audience for managers

**13.** When is Publish to web appropriate for a Charles River report?

A.  When the readers cannot get a Power BI license
B.  When the report uses row-level security
C.  When the data may be made public
D.  When the report is a monitoring page

**14.** The package is published from a file that reads CharlesRiver.xlsx on a local drive. What does a scheduled refresh in the Power BI service need?

A.  An on-premises data gateway that can reach the file
B.  A Premium Per User license for each reader of the report
C.  A sensitivity label on the semantic model
D.  A row-level security role for the refresh

**15.** Viewed as a department manager, the Income Statement page shows only that cost center's rows and nothing on it says so. Which response fits the chapter's recommendations?

A.  Hide the page so that it no longer appears among the page tabs of the report
B.  Move it to a separate report for finance, and label what each manager sees
C.  Add an object-level security rule to the Income Statement page
D.  Remove the CostCenter rule so that managers see the whole ledger

<!-- Answer key, Chapter 16:
     1 C, 2 A, 3 D, 4 B, 5 A, 6 C, 7 B, 8 D, 9 B, 10 C, 11 D, 12 A, 13 C, 14 A, 15 B
     1 C: continuous monitoring is management's ongoing review of its own controls (Tronto & Killingsworth, 2021).
     2 A: rule tests produce exceptions; analytical tests produce anomalies (Kogan et al., 2014).
     3 D: with a weak system, early notification increased the inclination to commit fraud (Gonzalez & Hoffman, 2018).
     4 B: unpivoting turns the selected columns into Attribute and Value rows.
     5 A: Append matches by name, so OrderDate becomes its own column and EventDate stays null for orders.
     6 C: rates need populations; a count alone hides volume (hundreds of entries against thousands of orders).
     7 B: an exception in every period points to design (one approver approves every register, including the approver's own).
     8 D: a rule filters its table and, through active relationships, the many side.
     9 B: row-level security applies to Viewers and app readers, not to Admin, Member, or Contributor.
     10 C: managers of record 81, 83, 85 are terminated; the Sales and Warehouse Managers are not recorded.
     11 D: deny by default; a user in the role but missing from the table sees no sales (and no cost centers).
     12 A: object-level security hides tables and columns from a role; row-level security hides rows.
     13 C: Publish to web needs no sign-in, exposes all the model's data, and does not support row-level security.
     14 A: a local file is an on-premises source; a gateway (or moving the file to OneDrive or SharePoint) is needed.
     15 B: pages cannot be secured by role; app audiences show whole reports, so finance's pages go in a separate report,
          and a card naming the cost centers shown tells managers what they see. Hiding a page is not security. -->
